summary: TypeScript framework for building AI agents and workflows, with model routing to 40+ providers, memory, RAG, MCP, evals and observability.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Mastra is a TypeScript framework for building AI applications and agents. It covers agents that use tools, a graph-based workflow engine, human-in-the-loop pauses, memory and retrieval, MCP server authoring, evals and observability. It plugs into React, Next.js and Node apps or can be deployed as a standalone server.
sixtySeconds.problem: Building production agents in TypeScript means gluing together model SDKs, tools, workflows, memory and monitoring. Mastra provides them in one framework.
whoFor: Teams shipping agents in Next.js or Node apps
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a TypeScript-first stack that goes from prototype to production, with one interface to models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and more.
requirements: An API key for a model provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or xAI for the starter)

overview: Create a project with npm create mastra@latest and follow the prompts, or see the installation guide for a manual setup. The starter creates a default project, installs Mastra skills for coding assistants it detects and sets up Git.
Agents reason about goals, pick tools and iterate; workflows give explicit control with steps you chain together. Workflows and agents can pause for user approval and resume later.
Templates, a course and videos help beginners. The core is Apache 2.0; code in ee/ folders is under the Mastra Enterprise License.
limitations: Enterprise features need a license in production
